title: Metallic Circles: Concyclic Tangency Points of Ford Circles over k-Fibonacci Quotients
method: read in full (arXiv HTML v1); statements formalised by hand, as printed

definitions.name: p6_kfib
definitions.lean: noncomputable def p6_kfib (k : ℤ) (n : ℤ) : ℤ := ((!![k, 1; 1, 0] : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ) ^ n) 0 1
definitions.notes: k-Fibonacci numbers with integer index; consistency with the paper's recurrence is p6_kfib_def

statements.label: Definition (Sec 2.2)
statements.name: p6_kfib_def
statements.original: f_0=0, f_1=1, f_{n+1}=k f_n+f_{n-1}; negative indices by f_{n-1}=f_{n+1}-k f_n
statements.lean: (k n : ℤ) : p6_kfib k 0 = 0 ∧ p6_kfib k 1 = 1 ∧ p6_kfib k (n + 1) = k * p6_kfib k n + p6_kfib k (n - 1)
statements.notes: Checks that the library definition p6_kfib (entry (0,1) of M^n) satisfies the paper's defining recurrence for every integer n; this characterises it uniquely. Stated for all integers k (paper: k>=1).

statements.label: Eq. (3) (Sec 2.2)
statements.name: p6_kfib_matrix
statements.lean: (k n : ℤ) : (!![k, 1; 1, 0] : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℤ) ^ n = !![p6_kfib k (n + 1), p6_kfib k n; p6_kfib k n, p6_kfib k (n - 1)]
statements.notes: Integer matrix power (zpow, inverse for negative n).

statements.label: Sec 2.2 (unnumbered)
statements.name: p6_kfib_neg
statements.lean: (k : ℤ) (m : ℕ) : p6_kfib k (-(m : ℤ)) = (-1) ^ (m + 1) * p6_kfib k (m : ℤ)
statements.notes: m taken as a natural number (the paper says 'by induction').

statements.label: Proof of Lemma 2.3 (unnumbered)
statements.name: p6_addition
statements.original: f_{m+n} = f_m f_{n+1} + f_{m-1} f_n and companion f_{m+n+1} = f_{m+1} f_{n+1} + f_m f_n
statements.lean: (k m n : ℤ) : p6_kfib k (m + n) = p6_kfib k m * p6_kfib k (n + 1) + p6_kfib k (m - 1) * p6_kfib k n ∧ p6_kfib k (m + n + 1) = p6_kfib k (m + 1) * p6_kfib k (n + 1) + p6_kfib k m * p6_kfib k n

statements.label: Lemma 2.3 (6)
statements.name: p6_lem23_eq6
statements.lean: (k n : ℤ) : p6_kfib k (2 * n) = p6_kfib k n * (p6_kfib k (n - 1) + p6_kfib k (n + 1))

statements.label: Lemma 2.3 (7)
statements.name: p6_lem23_eq7
statements.lean: (k n : ℤ) : p6_kfib k (2 * n + 1) = p6_kfib k n ^ 2 + p6_kfib k (n + 1) ^ 2

statements.label: Lemma 2.3 (8) Cassini
statements.name: p6_lem23_eq8
statements.lean: (k n : ℤ) : p6_kfib k (n - 1) * p6_kfib k (n + 1) - p6_kfib k n ^ 2 = ((Int.negOnePow n : ℤˣ) : ℤ)
statements.notes: (-1)^n for integer n is Mathlib's Int.negOnePow.

statements.label: Lemma 2.3 (9)
statements.name: p6_lem23_eq9
statements.lean: (k n : ℤ) : p6_kfib k (n + 1) ^ 2 - k * p6_kfib k n * p6_kfib k (n + 1) - p6_kfib k n ^ 2 = ((Int.negOnePow n : ℤˣ) : ℤ)

statements.label: Lemma 2.3 (10) d'Ocagne
statements.name: p6_lem23_eq10
statements.lean: (k a b : ℤ) : p6_kfib k a * p6_kfib k (b + 1) - p6_kfib k (a + 1) * p6_kfib k b = ((Int.negOnePow b : ℤˣ) : ℤ) * p6_kfib k (a - b)

statements.label: After Lemma 2.3 (unnumbered)
statements.name: p6_coprime
statements.lean: (k n : ℤ) : IsCoprime (p6_kfib k n) (p6_kfib k (n + 1))

statements.label: Sec 3 (unnumbered)
statements.name: p6_odd_pos
statements.original: Note that f_{2n+1} > 0, since it is a sum of squares

statements.label: Proposition 2.1 (Ford), first half
statements.name: p6_prop21_tangent
statements.original: If det [[p,r],[q,s]] = ±1 then K[p,q] and K[r,s] are tangent
statements.notes: Tangent = externally tangent: distance of centres equals sum of radii; stated as an iff (stronger than printed). Finite circles only (q,s>0); the K[1,0] line convention is not formalised. Cited result (Ford 1938). 只覆盖两个有限 Ford 圆（分母都为正）；论文按约定还包括无穷远圆 K[1,0]（直线 y=1），该情形见 p6_prop21_inf_tangent（独立复核 review-p6-b 指出后补充）

statements.label: Proposition 2.1 (Ford), second half
statements.name: p6_prop21_disjoint
statements.original: two distinct Ford circles ... otherwise, they are disjoint
statements.notes: Distinct circles read as p/q ≠ r/s i.e. ps-qr ≠ 0; disjoint = distance of centres exceeds sum of radii. Reducedness of the fractions is not needed. 只覆盖两个有限 Ford 圆（分母都为正）；论文按约定还包括无穷远圆 K[1,0]（直线 y=1），该情形见 p6_prop21_inf_disjoint（独立复核 review-p6-b 指出后补充）

statements.label: Proposition 2.2 (Kocik), formula (1)
statements.name: p6_prop22_on_circles
statements.original: If K[p,q] and K[r,s] are tangent, their tangency point is ((pq+rs)/(q^2+s^2), 1/(q^2+s^2))
statements.notes: The point (1) lies on both circles. 只覆盖两个有限 Ford 圆（分母都为正）；论文按约定还包括无穷远圆 K[1,0]（直线 y=1），该情形见 p6_prop22_inf_point（独立复核 review-p6-b 指出后补充）

statements.label: Proposition 2.2 (Kocik), uniqueness
statements.name: p6_prop22_unique
statements.original: ...their tangency point is (1)
statements.notes: Any common point of the two tangent circles is the point (1). 只覆盖两个有限 Ford 圆（分母都为正）；论文按约定还包括无穷远圆 K[1,0]（直线 y=1），该情形见 p6_prop22_inf_point（独立复核 review-p6-b 指出后补充）

statements.label: Theorem 3.1 (Metallic circle)
statements.name: p6_thm31_circle
statements.original: the points P_n=(f_{2n}/f_{2n+1}, 1/f_{2n+1}), n in Z, lie on C_k: (x+k/2)^2+y^2=(k^2+4)/4
statements.notes: Stated for every integer k (paper: k>=1; the hypothesis is not needed).

statements.label: Theorem 3.1, feet
statements.name: p6_thm31_feet
statements.original: C_k meets the X-axis at (σ_k^{-1},0) and (-σ_k,0)
statements.notes: Read as: the points of C_k on the axis are exactly these two.

statements.label: Corollary 3.2, monotonicity
statements.name: p6_cor32_mono
statements.original: the abscissa x_n=f_{2n}/f_{2n+1} of P_n is strictly increasing in n in Z
statements.lean: (k : ℤ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : StrictMono (fun n : ℤ => ((p6_kfib k (2 * n) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ((p6_kfib k (2 * n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ))

statements.label: Corollary 3.2 (12), n→+∞
statements.name: p6_cor32_lim_top
statements.lean: (k : ℤ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℤ => ((p6_kfib k (2 * n) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ((p6_kfib k (2 * n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds ((((k : ℝ) + Real.sqrt ((k : ℝ) ^ 2 + 4)) / 2)⁻¹)) ∧ Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℤ => 1 / ((p6_kfib k (2 * n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ)) Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

statements.label: Corollary 3.2 (12), n→-∞
statements.name: p6_cor32_lim_bot
statements.lean: (k : ℤ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) : Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℤ => ((p6_kfib k (2 * n) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ((p6_kfib k (2 * n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ)) Filter.atBot (nhds (-(((k : ℝ) + Real.sqrt ((k : ℝ) ^ 2 + 4)) / 2))) ∧ Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℤ => 1 / ((p6_kfib k (2 * n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ)) Filter.atBot (nhds 0)

statements.label: Proposition 3.3, first sentence
statements.name: p6_prop33_ford
statements.original: translation (x,y)→(x+j,y) and reflection (x,y)→(-x,y) preserve the family of Ford circles and map tangency points to tangency points
statements.notes: Formalised at the level of the labels: K[p,q]→K[p+jq,q], K[p,q]→K[-p,q]; determinant preserved up to sign and formula (1) transforms accordingly.

statements.label: Proposition 3.3, chain
statements.name: p6_prop33_chain
statements.original: translated point (f_{2n+2}/f_{2n+1},1/f_{2n+1}); reflected point with index n is the translated point with index -n-1; they lie on the circle with centre (k/2,0) and radius r_k

statements.label: Proposition 3.3, feet
statements.name: p6_prop33_feet
statements.original: which meets the axis at (σ_k,0) and (-σ_k^{-1},0)

statements.label: Remark 3.4
statements.name: p6_rem34
statements.original: the symmetry (x,y)→(-k-x,y) swaps P_n and P_{-n-1}

statements.label: Lemma 3.5
statements.name: p6_lem35
statements.original: p/q, r/s fractions with ps-qr=±1, a>=1 integer, (u,v)=a(r,s)+(p,q); T, T' tangency points of K[p,q],K[r,s] and K[r,s],K[u,v]: d_H(T,T') = 2 arcsinh(a/2)
statements.notes: Tangency points given by formula (1); d_H is Mathlib's hyperbolic distance on the upper half-plane. As printed there are no sign conditions on q, s, v (the formula (1) is used also for q=0 / negative denominators, per the paper's footnote).

statements.label: Proof of Corollary 3.6
statements.name: p6_arsinh_metallic
statements.original: arcsinh(k/2) = ln σ_k
statements.lean: (k : ℤ) : Real.arsinh ((k : ℝ) / 2) = Real.log (((k : ℝ) + Real.sqrt ((k : ℝ) ^ 2 + 4)) / 2)

statements.label: Corollary 3.6 (Equidistance)
statements.name: p6_cor36
statements.original: d_H(P_m,P_n) = 2|m-n| ln σ_k, m,n in Z
statements.lean: (k : ℤ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (m n : ℤ) (P Q : UpperHalfPlane) (hP : (P : ℂ) = ⟨((p6_kfib k (2 * m) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ((p6_kfib k (2 * m + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ), 1 / ((p6_kfib k (2 * m + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ)⟩) (hQ : (Q : ℂ) = ⟨((p6_kfib k (2 * n) : ℤ) : ℝ) / ((p6_kfib k (2 * n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ), 1 / ((p6_kfib k (2 * n + 1) : ℤ) : ℝ)⟩) : dist P Q = 2 * |((m - n : ℤ) : ℝ)| * Real.log (((k : ℝ) + Real.sqrt ((k : ℝ) ^ 2 + 4)) / 2)

statements.label: Proposition 2.1 (Ford), circle at infinity, tangency
statements.name: p6_prop21_inf_tangent
statements.original: K[1,0] is the line y=1; K[p,q], K[r,s] tangent iff det(p r; q s) = ±1 (here p=1, q=0)
statements.notes: K[r,s] has centre height 1/(2s^2) and radius 1/(2s^2); the line y=1 is tangent to it iff the gap 1 - 1/(2s^2) equals the radius. Determinant written literally for (p,q)=(1,0).

statements.label: Proposition 2.1 (Ford), circle at infinity, disjointness
statements.name: p6_prop21_inf_disjoint
statements.original: otherwise (det ≠ ±1) the circles are disjoint
statements.notes: Disjoint from the line y=1 means the radius is smaller than the distance from the centre to the line.

statements.label: Proposition 2.2 (Kocik), circle at infinity
statements.name: p6_prop22_inf_point
statements.original: formula (1) gives (r,1) for the tangency of K[1,0] with K[r,1]
statements.notes: First conjunct: formula (1) with (p,q,r,s)=(1,0,r,1) evaluates to (r,1). Second: (r,1) is the unique common point of the line y=1 and K[r,1].
